text: Right to confirm whether or not a controller is processing the consumer's personal data and to access such personal data (§ 59.1-577(A)(1)).
Right to correct inaccuracies in the consumer's personal data, taking into account the nature of the personal data and the purposes of the processing (§ 59.1-577(A)(2)).
Right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer (§ 59.1-577(A)(3)).
Right to obtain a copy of the consumer's personal data previously provided to the controller in a portable and, to the extent technically feasible, readily usable format (§ 59.1-577(A)(4)).

Right to opt out of the processing of personal data for purposes of (i) targeted advertising, (ii) the sale of personal data, or (iii) profiling in furtherance of decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning the consumer (§ 59.1-577(A)(5)).

Respond to the consumer without undue delay, but in all cases within 45 days of receipt of the request; extendable once by 45 additional days when reasonably necessary if the consumer is informed within the initial period together with the reason (§ 59.1-577(B)(1)).

Provide information in response to a consumer request free of charge up to twice annually; a reasonable fee may be charged or the request declined if manifestly unfounded, excessive, or repetitive, with the burden on the controller. Where the controller cannot authenticate the request using commercially reasonable efforts it need not comply and may request additional information (§ 59.1-577(B)(3), (B)(4)).

Establish a conspicuously available process for a consumer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action, and inform the consumer in writing within 60 days of receipt of an appeal of any action taken or not taken, including a written explanation of the reasons and, if denied, a method to contact the Attorney General (§ 59.1-577(C)).
Limit the collection of personal data to what is adequate, relevant, and reasonably necessary in relation to the disclosed purposes for which such data is processed (§ 59.1-578(A)(1)).
Not process personal data for purposes that are neither reasonably necessary to nor compatible with the disclosed purposes, unless the controller obtains the consumer's consent (§ 59.1-578(A)(2)).
Establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices appropriate to the volume and nature of the personal data at issue (§ 59.1-578(A)(3)).
Not process personal data in violation of state and federal anti-discrimination laws, and not discriminate against a consumer for exercising consumer rights (§ 59.1-578(A)(4)).

Not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent, or, for sensitive data concerning a known child, without processing in accordance with COPPA (§ 59.1-578(A)(5)).

Provide consumers with a reasonably accessible, clear, and meaningful privacy notice containing the categories of personal data processed, the purpose for processing, how to exercise and appeal consumer rights, the categories of personal data shared with third parties, and the categories of those third parties (§ 59.1-578(C)).

Where the controller sells personal data to third parties or processes personal data for targeted advertising, clearly and conspicuously disclose such processing and the manner in which a consumer may exercise the right to opt out (§ 59.1-578(D)).

Establish, and describe in a privacy notice, one or more secure and reliable means for consumers to submit rights requests; consumers shall not be required to create a new account to exercise rights (§ 59.1-578(E)).
Not sell or offer for sale precise geolocation data concerning a consumer (§ 59.1-578(A)(6)).

Comply with the limits on processing personal data collected from a known child, including prohibitions on targeted advertising, sale, and profiling, retention limits, and restrictions on collecting precise geolocation data, absent parental consent obtained in accordance with COPPA (§ 59.1-578(F)).
A processor shall adhere to the instructions of a controller and shall assist the controller in meeting its obligations under this chapter (§ 59.1-579(A)).

Assist the controller, by appropriate technical and organizational measures insofar as reasonably practicable, in fulfilling the controller's obligation to respond to consumer rights requests (§ 59.1-579(A)(1)).

Assist the controller in meeting its obligations in relation to the security of processing and in relation to the notification of a breach of security of the system of the processor pursuant to § 18.2-186.6 (§ 59.1-579(A)(2)).
Provide necessary information to enable the controller to conduct and document data protection assessments pursuant to § 59.1-580 (§ 59.1-579(A)(3)).

Execute a binding contract governing the processor's data processing procedures that sets forth instructions for processing, the nature and purpose of processing, the type of data, the duration of processing, and the rights and obligations of both parties, and that requires confidentiality, deletion or return of data, demonstration of compliance, cooperation with assessments, and written subcontractor flow-down (§ 59.1-579(B)).
Conduct and document a data protection assessment of the processing of personal data for purposes of targeted advertising (§ 59.1-580(A)(1)).
Conduct and document a data protection assessment of the sale of personal data (§ 59.1-580(A)(2)).

Conduct and document a data protection assessment of the processing of personal data for purposes of profiling, where such profiling presents a reasonably foreseeable risk of unfair or deceptive treatment or unlawful disparate impact, financial, physical, or reputational injury, offensive intrusion upon solitude or seclusion, or other substantial injury to consumers (§ 59.1-580(A)(3)).
Conduct and document a data protection assessment of the processing of sensitive data (§ 59.1-580(A)(4)).
Conduct and document a data protection assessment of any processing activities involving personal data that present a heightened risk of harm to consumers (§ 59.1-580(A)(5)).

Conduct a data protection assessment for any online service, product, or feature directed to consumers the controller has actual knowledge are children, addressing its purpose, the categories of known children's personal data processed, and the purposes of that processing (§ 59.1-580(B)).
Take reasonable measures to ensure that de-identified data cannot be associated with a natural person (§ 59.1-581(A)(1)).
Publicly commit to maintaining and using de-identified data without attempting to re-identify the data (§ 59.1-581(A)(2)).
Contractually obligate any recipients of the de-identified data to comply with all provisions of this chapter (§ 59.1-581(A)(3)).

Prior to initiating any action, the Attorney General shall provide a controller or processor 30 days' written notice identifying the specific provisions alleged to have been violated; no action shall be initiated if the violation is cured within that period and an express written statement is provided (§ 59.1-584(B)).

Following an uncured violation or a breach of the express written statement, the Attorney General may seek an injunction and civil penalties of up to $7,500 for each violation, plus reasonable expenses and attorney fees (§ 59.1-584(C), (D)).
